title: ‘Opportunity for Shared Commitment to Improve Future of Our Cities’: Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Opens ARISE Cities Forum 2026
subtitle:
Second edition of the forum brings together 200+ delegates from 50+ cities across 18+ countries representing the Global South.

Discussions must lead to practical actions that cities can adopt, says MoS.
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The second edition of the ARISE Cities Forum opened today at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi today. The two-day Forum is being organised by ICLEI South Asia, in collaboration with the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), with support from the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India.
Themed “
From Bharat to Antalya — Commit. Implement. Deliver,
” the Forum features
3 technical plenaries and 14 technical sessions
, focusing on the experiences of local governments from the Global South region in advancing urban resilience, sustainability, and equitable and low-carbon development. The discussions feed into the
Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals 2026
, which will be adopted on 28 October, 2026 at the forum and presented at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.
The Inaugural Ceremony of the Forum was graced by
Shri Tokhan Sahu
, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India;
Shoko Ishikawa
, Country Representative, UN Women India;
Dr Debolina Kundu
, Director, National Institute of Urban Affairs;
Gino Van Begin
, Secretary General, ICLEI; and
Emani Kumar
, Deputy Secretary General, ICLEI and Executive Director, ICLEI South Asia.
Also present were
Adv. Minimol V.K
, Hon’ble Mayor of Kochi, India;
Ismail Rafeeq
, Hon’ble Mayor of Fuvahmulah, Maldives;
Bhola Pokhrel
, Hon’ble Mayor of Karjanha, Nepal; and
Thinley Namgay
, Hon’ble Mayor of Samdrup Jongkhar, Bhutan, representing urban leadership from across South Asia.
Appreciating the progress made since the first edition of the Forum, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs
Shri Tokhan Sahu
called for collective efforts to develop sustainable cities to fulfil India’s climate commitments and realise the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
“From resolve to planning, from planning to implementation, and from implementation to results—that should be our way of working. Our goal is to build cities where development reaches every section of society and creates better opportunities for future generations,”
he said.
Calling for gender-responsive and inclusive urban development, Country Representative, UN Women India
Shoko Ishikawa
stated, “
Drawing on the lessons gained from our initiatives in India, there are three priorities: integrate gender equality into urban planning, climate policies and investments; invest in urban infrastructure and services that strengthen women's safety, mobility and economic participation; and institutionalise women's leadership and accountability in urban climate action.”
She added that UN Women looks forward to working with the ARISE Cities Forum to carry this agenda forward so that women and girls help shape the cities of tomorrow.
Director of the National Institute of Urban Affairs,
Dr Debolina Kundu
, noted that the theme of this year's Forum, "From Bharat to Antalya – Commit, Implement, Deliver," reflects the urgency of moving from climate commitments to action. “
As we look towards COP31, it is important that the experiences, priorities and solutions emerging from our cities find a stronger place in national and global climate conversations
,” she remarked.
Secretary General of ICLEI,
Gino Van Begin
, also spoke of the potential of urban local governments, stating, “
Cities are developing innovative solutions, building functioning partnerships and demonstrating pathways towards more resilient, inclusive and sustainable futures. Their experiences and priorities must have a stronger voice in global processes such as the UNFCCC COPs, and this is what the ARISE Cities Forum aims to achieve.
”
Emphasising the purpose of the Forum, Deputy Secretary General, ICLEI and Executive Director, ICLEI South Asia,
Emani Kumar
said, “
The ARISE Cities Forum aims to amplify voices from the Global South so they are heard ‘from Bharat to Antalya’. We will carry the Delhi Declaration, a key outcome of our collective efforts and a shared call for stronger local climate action, to the global stage at COP31 to make sure that the perspectives and priorities of our cities and urban stakeholders are heard loud and clear.
”
Advancing sustainable, equitable and resilient cities Across the Global South: Takeaways from Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum 2026
Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 featured 2 Plenary sessions and 8 technical sessions. The discussions, featuring high-level representatives from city governments, state-level bodies, embassies, UN agencies, development institutions, and experts, spanned topics such as
the need for strengthening multilevel action to translate global climate commitments into measurable action on the ground,
climate-resilient water management and sustainable energy transition in cities,
advancing urban biodiversity and nature-positive cities,
positioning entertainment and culture as an actionable lever for systemic urban resilience,
building resilient coastal cities and communities, and
integrating public health and child- and youth-focused initiatives with climate-resilient urban planning.
The
winners of the Youth for Climate Hackathon 2.0
were also felicitated with the Ritu Thakur Memorial Award on Day 1 of the Forum. The Hackathon invited solutions on ‘Action-Oriented Transition: Translating Resilient, Scalable, and Inclusive Solutions for Circular Cities’ by young innovators from countries in South Asia.
A Memorandum of Understanding was also exchanged between Global Buildings Performance Network (GBPN) and ICLEI South Asia.
Launches on Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum
The Inaugural and technical sessions on 27 October also featured the launch of the following:
The Centre for Sustainable Urban Mobility and Integrated Transportation (SUMMIT)
Investing in Climate Resilient Cities - State-Level Project Pipelines: Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh & Telangana
reports
Embedding Gender Equity and Responsive Transport - A Compendium of Case Studies for Gender and Mobility in India
A Compendium of Case Studies for Mobilising Funds to Enable Integrated Planning and Infrastructure Development
Policy Framework for Gender Equality in Public Bus Transport Systems
Guidelines on Canal Restoration using Nature-based Solutions
Poster for the ‘Early Action for Children’s Health (EACH): Towards Heat Resilience and Clean Air’ project in collaboration with UNICEF India
ICLEI South Asia’s Annual Report for 2025–26
Looking ahead to COP31
The Forum will continue on 28 October, with one Plenary, six technical sessions, and the Closing Ceremony, where the
Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals 2026
will be adopted and handed over to
Samed Ağırbaş, COP31 Climate Champion and President of the Zero Waste Foundation.
The Declaration will mark
a key milestone in carrying the ARISE Cities Forum’s collective commitments and urban priorities forward to COP31 in Antalya, strengthening the presence of cities from the Global South on the global climate stage.
For more information on the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 and its agenda, please visit:
https://arisecitiesforum.org/

content:
A two-day State-Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme, “Shram Samvad”, on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection was jointly organized by Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE), Government of India (GoI) and Labour Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh (GoUP) at Taj Hotel, Lucknow on 26th and 27th October, 2026.
The programme was aimed at enhancing awareness among employers, HR, Legal and Finance professionals regarding the new Labour Codes and rules made thereunder. It also focused on strengthening awareness and institutional capacity on labour reforms, welfare and social protection, and promoting Centre-State coordination, stakeholder engagement as well as technology-enabled delivery of labour and employment services. The programme was attended by senior officials from MoLE, Labour Department, GoUP, Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) [CLC (C)], Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Directorate General Labour Welfare (DGLW) along with employers, industry representatives, and legal, HR and finance professionals.
Day 1: Context-Setting, Keynote Address & Technical Sessions
The first day focused on labour reforms, social protection and the State labour ecosystem.
Shri Anil Rajbhar, Minister for Labour and Employment, GoUP
, addressed the programme.
Dr. Ashish Kumar Goel, Additional Chief Secretary, Labour & Employment, GoUP
, delivered the welcome address and set the context for the programme.
Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar
,
Secretary, Labour & Employment, Government of India,
delivered the keynote address, highlighting the transformative potential of the Labour Codes, Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) welfare, social protection, technology-enabled service delivery and stronger Centre-State collaboration.
Technical sessions covered implementation of the Labour Codes in Uttar Pradesh; convergence of social protection schemes and extension of coverage to unorganised, gig and platform workers; BOCW registration, cess and welfare benefits; international mobility; State best practices; ESIC and EPFO initiatives; and digital platforms including e-Shram, Shram Suvidha Portal, SAMADHAN Portal and Labour Stack. The sessions were addressed by senior representatives of the MoLE, Govt. of UP, ESIC and EPFO.
Day 2: Implementation of Labour Codes and Way Forward
The second day was attended by employers, industry representatives, and legal, HR and finance professionals. Shri Manohar Lal Mannu Kori, Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Government of Uttar Pradesh addressed the participants. The technical session on the Labour Codes was chaired by
Shri Alok Chandra, Principal Labour Economics Adviser (PLEA), Ministry of Labour & Employment. Dr. P. K. Jena, Director (Labour Reforms), MoLE,
presented an overview of the Labour Codes, followed by an address by Sessions on compliances under the Code on Wages, 2019, Industrial Relations Code, 2020, Code on Social Security, 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. The sessions were presented by senior representatives of MoLE and Govt. of UP
.
The discussions focused on practical compliance requirements and implementation issues under the four Labour Codes.
The programme also included sessions on the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY), moderated by
Ms. Richa Sharma, Director, MoLE;
and addressed by Shri Uday Baxi, ACC, EPFO, and the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana (PM-SYM), addressed by
Shri Pradyumn Kumar Rana, Welfare Commissioner, DGLW, MoLE
. Thereafter, an open Q&A session provided participants an opportunity to seek clarifications on the provisions, implementation and compliance requirements under the Labour Codes and Rules.
A dedicated session on prevention, rescue, rehabilitation, convergence and district-level monitoring of child labour, along with identification, release, rehabilitation and interdepartmental coordination for bonded labour, was presented by
Shri Syed Rizwan Ali, State Coordinator, Child Labour. Shri Ashok Kumar, Retired IAS,
presented the
Veilpur
experience of sustained elimination of child labour and discussed strategies for total elimination and rehabilitation.
To facilitate the employers and professions in effective implementation of the Labour Codes and Rules,
‘Handbook of Compliance for Employers’ and ‘Compilation of Frequently Asked Questions’
developed by MoLE were also shared with the participants. Open house sessions to address questions and queries from participants and address the gaps in understanding provisions of Codes and Rules as well as social security schemes were also held on both days, and more than 100 questions were deliberated.
The programme concluded with closing remarks and a vote of thanks by
Shri Kunal Silku, Special Secretary, Labour & Employment, Govt. of UP.
The programme reaffirmed the need for coordinated action, simplified compliance, technology-driven delivery and stronger convergence to ensure effective implementation of labour reforms and wider social protection. Uttar Pradesh gave assurance of their intent to conduct similar Shram Samvad programmes in other industrial districts of the State.

Two industrial disputes involving the management of Bihar Gramin Bank and its employees’ organisations were amicably resolved on October 22 and 23, 2026, through conciliation efforts of the Assistant Labour Commissioner (Central), Patna, under the Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.
The settlements are expected to extend financial benefits amounting to approximately ₹77.69 crore to over 10,900 employees of Bihar Gramin Bank, including recurring annual benefits of approximately ₹9.02 crore under the settlement with the Bihar Gramin Bank Workers Organisation (BGBWO).
The first settlement, reached on October 22, 2026, between the Bihar Gramin Bank Adhikari Sangh, Patna, and the bank management, is expected to benefit around 8,400 employees, with financial benefits amounting to approximately ₹67.17 crore. The second settlement, reached on October 23, 2026, between the Bihar Gramin Bank Workers Organisation (BGBWO) and the bank management, is expected to benefit around 2,500 employees, with financial benefits amounting to approximately ₹10.52 crore, including recurring annual benefits of approximately ₹9.02 crore. This settlement addresses key demands relating to the effective implementation of the 12th Bipartite Settlement, enhancement of House Rent Allowance (HRA), increase in transport allowance for Divyang employees, payment of overtime, transparency in promotion processes and the formation of a Negotiating Council.
Both settlements were facilitated through constructive dialogue and the active participation and cooperation of the employees’ organisations and the bank management, helping resolve the disputes amicably and strengthen industrial harmony.

subtitle: ETM 2026 expands its scale, bringing together 1500+ delegates to advance energy innovation and commercialisation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 9:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 29th Energy Technology Meet (ETM 2026) was inaugurated today at the ONGC Advanced Training Institute in Goa by Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri. The three-day event brings together policymakers, industry leaders, researchers, technology providers and energy experts to discuss innovations shaping India’s energy future.
Organised by the Centre for High Technology (CHT) under the aegis of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India, and co-hosted by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), the meet is themed “Accelerating Energy Innovation: From Research to Commercialisation.” The platform aims to strengthen collaboration across the energy value chain and accelerate the development and commercial adoption of emerging technologies.
This is the largest ETM edition so far, with over 2,500 delegates, more than 250 speakers, 44 technical sessions and over 220 exhibition stalls.
During a fireside chat at the event, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri discussed how India responded to disruptions in global energy supply while seeking to protect consumers from the full impact of the crisis. He highlighted the importance of acting across domestic production, alternative imports and last-mile delivery, noting that LPG production was increased significantly to support household requirements. The discussion also underlined the role of coordination across oil and gas public sector undertakings, refineries and distribution networks in maintaining continuity of essential fuel supplies.
The conversation also focused on strengthening India’s long-term energy resilience through diversified supply sources, greater domestic production and a wider basket of fuels. The Minister highlighted the potential of compressed biogas (CBG) to turn agricultural residue and organic waste into energy while creating additional value for farmers and rural communities. Opportunities in sustainable aviation fuel and other next-generation biofuels were also discussed, alongside the need to strengthen domestic research, support start-ups and bring Indian technologies from development and pilot stages to commercial deployment.
He also discussed India’s response to disruptions in global energy supplies and the role of oil marketing companies (OMCs) in maintaining fuel availability. He highlighted how OMCs had navigated the West Asia crisis effectively, coordinating across refineries, supply networks and distribution channels to ensure continuity of essential fuel supplies. The discussion also covered measures to increase domestic LPG production, diversify import sources and protect consumers from the impact of global supply disruptions.
The Minister emphasized that India’s energy sourcing decisions were guided by its national interests and energy requirements. He highlighted that there are more than one lakh retail outlets in the country, but we managed to not let even a single RO go dry.
The conversation also explored ways to strengthen long-term energy resilience through greater domestic production and a diversified energy mix, including the potential of compressed biogas (CBG), opportunities in sustainable aviation fuel and next-generation biofuels, and the need to strengthen India’s research and development ecosystem to accelerate the commercialisation of indigenous energy technologies.
A key announcement at the event was the development of a National Oil and Gas R&D Vision following detailed consultations. To support its implementation, the government is establishing the National Hydrocarbon Technology Hub (NHTH), an expanded institutional platform to coordinate research and development across the sector.
The NHTH will subsume the existing Centre for High Technology (CHT) and operate with a broader mandate, bringing together central public sector enterprises, private-sector R&D, start-ups, MSMEs, academia, Centres of Excellence and research institutions around shared national priorities. The initiative is intended to strengthen coordination, reduce duplication and accelerate the development and deployment of globally competitive indigenous technologies—creating a more connected energy research ecosystem under the vision of “One Vision, One Ecosystem.”
The Minister also visited the exhibition, where technology providers, process licensors, engineering firms and energy companies showcased products, technologies and solutions for the downstream hydrocarbon sector. The exhibition offered stakeholders an opportunity to demonstrate technological advancements, exchange knowledge and explore solutions to emerging industry challenges.
The inaugural programme also highlighted government initiatives aimed at diversifying India’s energy mix and strengthening domestic energy production. GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, has an outlay of ₹23,731 crore for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 to scale up compressed biogas production and support the circular bioeconomy. Complementing these efforts, Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, has an approved outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to FY 2030–31 to boost oil and gas exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas and contribute to India’s long-term energy security.
The Minister also interacted with the media during a press conference, addressing issues relating to India’s energy landscape, including fuel availability, energy security, the energy transition and initiatives to diversify energy sources.
Running until October 29, ETM 2026 features technical presentations, panel discussions, poster sessions and an exhibition. Focus areas include green hydrogen, sustainable aviation fuel, carbon capture, crude-to-chemicals, biofuels, gas-based energy, refining technologies and digitalisation. The programme brings together experts from India and abroad to share research, exchange industry perspectives and identify opportunities to translate technological advances into commercially viable solutions.
The programme also features MC² Ignite, sessions on building a start-up ecosystem in India, and the Start-Up Awards and Refinery Performance & Innovation Awards, recognising technological advancements and innovation across the energy industry. An R&D Conclave by the Federation of Indian Petroleum Industry (FIPI) will focus on Net Zero refineries, energy efficiency, green hydrogen, biomass valorisation, water management and emerging technologies, while fostering collaboration across India’s energy sector.

title: Government of India Introduces Concessional Local Pass for National Highway Users Living Near Fee Plazas
subtitle: Eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a fee plaza can avail Concessional Local Pass for Rs. 1,500 per annum for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs. 3,000 per annum for fee plazas situated within these limits depending on the location of the plaza
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major step to enhance ‘Ease of Living’ for citizens residing near National Highway Fee Plazas, the Government of India has introduced a ‘Concessional Local Pass’ for eligible non-commercial vehicle owners residing within 20 km of a National Highway fee plaza. The rule will come into effect from 01st November 2026.
The annual fee for the concessional Local Pass will be Rs.1,500 for fee plazas located outside municipal or local town area and Rs.3,000 for toll plazas situated within these limits.
Under the new provision, eligible non-commercial vehicle owners with a valid and functional FASTag, residing within 20 km range can choose between the existing monthly pass and the concessional Local Pass for commuting through a specific fee plaza. The pass will be valid only for that fee plaza and will not be transferable to any other plazas.
The concessional Local Pass will not be available on National Highways or Expressways where toll fee collection is based on a closed user-fee collection system. It will also not be issued where a service road or alternative road is available for use by commuters.
The Annual Local Pass will be available at eligible Toll Plazas wef 01.11.2026. The Annual Local Pass will also be available through Rajmargyatra App wef 01.12.2026.
The amendment has been notified through the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the powers conferred by the National Highways Act, 1956. The rates may be revised by the Central Government annually with revisions taking effect on 01st April.
With over 13 crore FASTags issued across the country, the new provision aims to provide an option for eligible residents living near toll plazas to make travel more economical and enhance Ease of Commuting for local residents.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, organised a two-day Regional Rural Workshop under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G) in Lucknow on 27–28 October 2026. Held as a Samvad, it brought together States and field functionaries to deliberate on implementation and reforms.
Around 150 officials from Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Punjab, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and the host State of Uttar Pradesh are participating.
The workshop was graced by Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya, Hon’ble Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh; Shri Kamlesh Paswan, Hon’ble Minister of State for Rural Development, Government of India; and Smt. Vijay Lakshmi Gautam, Hon’ble Minister of State for Rural Development, Uttar Pradesh. Senior officials of the Ministry and the State Government were also present.
On the occasion, the dignitaries symbolically handed over house keys to PMAY-G beneficiaries of Uttar Pradesh as part of their “Grih Pravesh”.
With PMAY-G targeting 4.95 crore rural houses by March 2029, participants deliberated in detail on four proposed reforms for the next phase: cluster-based housing, strengthening of Rural Mason Training, Centres of Excellence, and a credit framework for rural housing. States shared their views on the feasibility, design and rollout of these reforms, while district and block functionaries from Uttar Pradesh presented field perspectives, highlighting ground-level challenges, good practices and the convergence and capacity needed for implementation.
This was followed by a State-wise review of progress, focusing on bottlenecks in house completion, timely release of instalments and construction quality. Technical and fund-flow issues relating to AwaasSoft and SNA-SPARSH were also discussed, including the need to ensure that eligible households are not inadvertently excluded during technology-enabled processes.
On the second day, the remaining States will present their progress, followed by a field visit to PMAY-G houses.
The workshop is expected to promote peer learning, address implementation bottlenecks and strengthen delivery of PMAY-G to eligible rural households.

title: India’s Genetic Diversity Could Make It a Global Destination for Gene Research: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh addresses Session on System and Synthetic Biology at ESTIC 2026, stressing India’s potential in gene research and biotechnology

India’s diverse genetic and phenotypic profile offers significant opportunities for scientific research and healthcare innovation

Focus on developing domestic gene-synthesis capabilities and strengthening India’s biotechnology ecosystem: Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, has said that India’s rich genetic diversity holds significant potential to make the country an important global resource for gene research, with other nations looking towards India for its unique genetic resources in the coming years.
Addressing a session on System and Synthetic Biology at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the need to build domestic capabilities in emerging areas of biotechnology and translate India’s scientific strengths into research opportunities and practical applications.
The Minister said India’s remarkable genetic and phenotypic diversity provides a valuable foundation for research, particularly in understanding variations in disease patterns and exploring new possibilities in healthcare. He expressed confidence that as India develops and scales up its research capabilities, the country can emerge as an important source of genetic resources for the global scientific community.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also stressed the importance of strengthening indigenous technological capabilities in gene synthesis. Dependence on overseas suppliers for specialised research requirements can create challenges for Indian scientists in terms of time, access and research continuity. Building domestic capabilities in this area would help researchers pursue their work more efficiently and strengthen the country’s biotechnology ecosystem.
The Minister said India has considerable scientific talent and that the government has accorded high priority to research and innovation. He emphasised the need to strengthen the support systems required to take research forward, including greater industry participation and funding for promising scientific work.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also spoke about the growing convergence of disciplines and the need to bring together biology, engineering, mathematics and other areas of expertise. Such interdisciplinary collaboration is becoming increasingly important as scientific research moves towards more complex applications and new technology pathways.
Referring to advances in nuclear medicine, the Minister discussed the importance of creating greater awareness about emerging research opportunities and enabling wider participation in the sector. He referred to provisions under the recently enacted SHANTI Act that open nuclear medicine research to private-sector participation, adding that such initiatives can create opportunities for further research and industry engagement.
The discussion also touched upon the need to strengthen the pathway from scientific discovery to technology development and practical application. Greater collaboration among research institutions, industry and entrepreneurs can help promising discoveries progress towards products and solutions that benefit society.
The session was included Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology (DBT), and brought together scientists and experts to discuss the potential of system and synthetic biology and the development of emerging biotechnology capabilities in India.
ESTIC 2026 brings together scientists, policymakers, industry leaders, start-ups and young researchers to strengthen the interface between scientific research, technological innovation and national development. The conclave provides a platform to explore emerging technologies, encourage collaboration and support the translation of scientific knowledge into practical applications.

content:

The Secretary toured and inspected the participating artisans’ stalls and the Ministry Pavilion.
The ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM) 2026 in Guwahati continues to attract visitors, providing a vibrant platform for traditional artisans to showcase and sell their handloom and handicraft products.
During his visit, the Secretary viewed the diverse range of traditional products on display and interacted with the artisans, gaining insights into their craftsmanship, products, and market opportunities.
He also visited the Ministry Pavilion, where information on the Ministry’s welfare, financial assistance, and development schemes is being disseminated to visitors through displays and informational material.
Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, the eight-day Mela commenced on October 21 and will continue until October 28, tomorrow.
The Mela is open to visitors from 11:00 AM to 9:00 PM and provides artisans with opportunities to connect directly with consumers, generate income, and explore avenues for expanding their businesses.
The Guwahati edition is the second Mela in the Shilp Samagam Series for the financial year 2026–27, following the successful conclusion of the first edition at Dasara Exhibition Grounds in Mysuru, Karnataka, on October 19, 2026.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Pant said the initiative promotes the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras, and Denotified Tribes (DNTs), in line with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi guided by the doctrine of
‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’.
The Secretary said a total of
75 artisans
, including
31 women artisans
, are participating in the Guwahati Mela, showcasing approximately
40 varieties
of handloom and handicraft products. The exhibits reflect India’s rich artistic traditions, indigenous skills, and regional diversity, with participation from the North-Eastern States and other parts of the country, he further said.
Shri Pant said the Mela provides artisans with a dedicated platform to display their products, engage directly with customers, and receive feedback on their offerings.
He said direct consumer interaction helps artisans understand market preferences, establish customer relationships, and identify opportunities to expand their reach. This initiative seeks to strengthen the connection between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary markets, enabling artisans to convert their skills into sustainable livelihood opportunities while preserving India’s rich cultural heritage, he added.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the daily cultural programmes featuring local and other artists, including music and dance performances representing the North-Eastern States, are adding to the Mela’s appeal.  said.
He said the performances provide visitors with an opportunity to experience the region’s cultural traditions alongside the country’s diverse handicrafts and handloom products. The cultural programmes are also being livestreamed to extend their reach beyond the physical venue, he said.
The Official said a dedicated Ministry Pavilion has been established at the Mela to disseminate information about the welfare, financial assistance, and development schemes of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The pavilion also showcases schemes and programmes implemented through the Ministry’s three National Corporations, enabling visitors to learn about the assistance and support available to eligible beneficiaries, he said.
The Official further informed that LED displays have been installed at the pavilion to screen informational content on the Ministry’s schemes and programmes. The initiative aims to enhance public awareness of government interventions supporting social and economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, and livelihood generation.
The pavilion complements the Mela’s market-oriented activities by bringing information about government schemes directly to visitors, including artisans and members of eligible communities who may benefit from these interventions.
The Official said a key focus of Shilp Samagam Mela is the promotion of
BHARAT-TULIP
(Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), which seeks to facilitate the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms.
By supporting access to wider markets and digital sales channels, the initiative aims to expand customer outreach, strengthen market linkages, and create additional opportunities for artisans to improve their earnings, he said.
The Official said it also supports the continued promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets. Through direct sales, consumer interaction, and exposure to a wider audience, the Mela encourages artisans to strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities and explore opportunities for sustained business growth, Official said.
Shilp Samagam Mela is an important initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the
National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC)
, the
National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC)
, and the
National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC)
.
By combining market access, public engagement, cultural promotion, and information dissemination, Shilp Samagam Mela seeks to strengthen entrepreneurship and facilitate sustainable livelihood opportunities for eligible communities. The visit of Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant underscores the importance of providing artisans with platforms to showcase their skills, connect with consumers, and explore opportunities for economic advancement.
Through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry continues its efforts to enhance the visibility of traditional products, promote market linkages, and support the socio-economic empowerment of artisans while preserving India’s rich handloom, handicraft, and cultural traditions.

title: Under NAMASTE Scheme, Union Minister of State Shri B. L. Verma Distributes PPE Kits And Ayushman Cards To Safai Mitras In Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh

date:

content:
Under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of Union Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, a major programme for the distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits and Ayushman Cards, was organised at Peeli Kothi Civil Lines area, in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, today.
The event was part of the ongoing flagship initiative aimed at strengthening the safety, health, and social security of Safai Mitras.
Hon’ble Minister of State, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, distributed the kits and cards among eligible beneficiaries.
The event was attended by Shri Anunaya Jha, District Magistrate, Moradabad; Shri Ram Gopal Anjan, Hon’ble Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC); Dr. Shaifali Singh Chauhan, District Panchayat Chairperson; the Municipal Commissioner, Moradabad; the Managing Director of the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC); officials from the concerned departments; and other dignitaries.

The Minister informed the a total of 90,194 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) have been verified so far, whileas 88,222 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers have been provided with PPE kits and 80,180 workers have been covered under health insurance through Ayushman Cards. In addition, 3,36,492 waste pickers have been profiled across the country, he further said.

title: Workshop on Base Revision of State -level Index of Industrial Production during 28–30 October 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) is convening a three Days Workshop on Base Revision of State-level Index of Industrial Production (IIP), at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam in collaboration with Department of Economics and Statistics (DES), Keralam during 28–30 October 2026.
The IIP is a key indicator of industrial performance, tracking changes in performance of industrial sector in economy. It is widely used by policymakers, economists, businesses and investors to assess trends in industrial activity and support informed decision-making. The index also serves as an important input in estimating overall economic growth.
MoSPI has updated the base year of the All-India IIP from 2011-12 to 2022-23. The base year is the reference year against which changes in production in later years are measured. A more recent base year helps the index reflect what India’s industries actually produce at present. The revised series incorporates several methodological improvements, including revision of the item basket and weights, updating of the factory panel, expansion of coverage to include activities such as Gas Supply, Water Supply, Sewerage and Waste Management and provision for factory substitution.
The State DES are responsible for compiling and disseminating the State-level IIP. As the nodal Ministry at the national level, the MoSPI provides technical guidance to States and Union Territories (UTs) to promote methodological uniformity and improve the quality and comparability of industrial statistics.
The three-day workshop will familiarise participating States and UTs with the proposed changes in the structure and methods of the revised IIP and help them finalise the list of items to be tracked and the factories that will report data. It will also provide a platform for discussions and feedback on the revisions to National Industrial Classification-2025 and National Product Classification.
Around 60 officials from MoSPI and the DESs of various States and UTs are expected to take part. Through this workshop, MoSPI aims to strengthen the quality, consistency and comparability of industrial statistics across the country.

subtitle: Fortnight-long nationwide drive to honour Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda and take flagship programmes to the last mile; 300+ projects, two national digital launches and 160+ State-level activities lined up

content:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs will observe Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada across the country from 1 to 15 November 2026, culminating in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas on 15 November, the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. More than a commemoration, the Pakhwada is a focused, time-bound drive to accelerate the Ministry's flagship programmes, take their benefits to tribal families at the last mile, and build awareness of schemes and entitlements among tribal communities, students and citizens.
The Government of India designated 15 November as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas in 2021 to commemorate the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The day honours the contribution of tribal heroes to India’s freedom struggle and the lasting place of tribal communities in the nation’s cultural, spiritual and social life. Since then, Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas has grown into a national movement that celebrates the resilience and cultural diversity of India’s tribal people, and has given momentum to transformative programmes such as PM-JANMAN and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan. During the previous 5 years, JJGD has been celebrated at Ranchi-2021, Khunti-2022 & 2023, Jamui-2024, and Dediapada-2025.
The 150th birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda was observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Varsh in 2024–25, with over 28 national-level events and more than 2 lakh activities that drew over 3.8 crore participants. For tribal communities, Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas stands for recognition of their role in the freedom struggle and of their knowledge, art and harmony with nature.
During the JJGD celebrations for this year (2026), the Ministry has lined up a series of national events through the fortnight. List of the events planned as below:
On 12 November, approximately 200 students of Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) will interact with the Hon'ble President at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
The National Tribal Literary Festival will be held at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, on 12 and 13 November with participation of Tribal writers from across the country,
National workshop at IIT Delhi “Strengthening Adi Vaani as Tribal Living Heritage and National Tribal Language Repository”.
The Rani Durgavati Adivasi Mahila Sammelan on 14 November will bring together 500 tribal women entrepreneurs from 30 States/UTs to strengthen market linkages and women-led enterprise.
The Swasthya–Poshan Sewa Sangam is holding health, nutrition and scheme camps for PVTGs at PM-JANMAN Multi-Purpose Centres from 15 October to 15 November.
Tribal Healers capacity building conclave with around 1,500 traditional healers from 9 States/UTs getting trained on 1 and 2 November in Hyderabad, under a programme to train and certify 1 lakh healers.
The Dharti Aaba Janbhagidari Abhiyan, through Adi Sewa Samay and Adi Sewa Din, will drive community participation in tribal villages, and about 1.54 lakh Adi Karmayogi Volunteers across 76,963 villages are being trained through State Administrative Training Institutes.
Scholarship Access Camps in 73 districts are assisting students with applications and Aadhaar seeding, and
Programme to conserve 200–300 medicinal plant species will be launched with CSIR-NBRI at Koraput, Odisha.
In addition to above, On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, over 300 projects for tribal communities across States will be taken up, with 228 ready for inauguration and 74 for foundation stone laying. These include a new Tribal Research Institute building in Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum at Kelsih, Mizoram.
Two national digital initiatives will also be launched. The Jan-HIT (Janjatiya Health Intelligence and Technology) Portal, developed with ICMR, is India's first platform for tribe-disaggregated health data, covering 20 States. The National FRA Digital Platform will bring the entire process of forest rights claims under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, from Gram Sabha submission to digitally signed titles, onto a single system.
Further, States and UTs are celebrating the Pakhwada through their Tribal Research Institutes, which have planned more than 160 activities in 19 States/UTs with an expected footfall of over 1 lakh people. These range from cultural festivals, exhibitions and tributes to competitions in schools, EMRS and hostels, and welfare and livelihood camps. Highlights include a statewide tribal carnival in Andhra Pradesh, the Adivasi Kala and Khel Samagam in Goa, a Bhagwan Birsa Munda Pavilion in Odisha, a Tribal Music Festival in Shillong and a tribal art and craft fair at Amdavad Haat, Gujarat. States will also hold Aadhaar and scholarship camps, sickle cell screening, Ayushman card camps for PVTGs, and legal literacy camps on forest rights.
The Ministry invites citizens to join the celebration by attending events in their area, taking part in the JJGD quiz and pledge on MyGov, supporting tribal artisans, and sharing their stories with #JanjatiyaGauravDivas and #JJGD2026.

The workshop reaffirmed CARA’s commitment to strengthening family-based care and expanding opportunities for children with special needs (Divyaang children) to find safe, permanent and loving families.
Organised as part of CARA’s continued efforts under the Adoption Awareness Campaign 2025, themed “Promoting Non-Institutionalised Rehabilitation of Children with Special Needs (Divyaang Children)”, the workshop focused on strengthening stakeholder convergence, addressing field-level challenges and identifying practical strategies to facilitate the adoption and rehabilitation of children with special needs.
The Eastern Zone, comprising Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Sikkim, represents a diverse geographical and administrative landscape. The workshop brought together approximately 175 stakeholders representing around 115 districts across Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal. It provided a vital platform for cross-sectoral dialogue, the exchange of best practices and the development of coordinated strategies to advance inclusive, family-based rehabilitation.
The workshop was graced by the presence of Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA; Shri Uma Shankar Singh, Secretary, DWCD&SS; Smt. Keerthishree G, State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities; Smt. Kiran Pasi, Director, Social Welfare, Jharkhand; Shri Bijay Kumar Sinha, Director and Member Secretary, JSCPS; and other senior officials.
Addressing the gathering, Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA, highlighted the encouraging progress achieved through focused outreach and stakeholder engagement. Emphasising the importance of sustained and collaborative efforts, she underlined the need to address the barriers that delay adoption and strengthen the support available to prospective adoptive parents. She further stressed that sustained awareness and a sensitive, child-centric approach are essential to enabling more children with special needs to find permanent families.
Shri Uma Shankar Singh, Secretary, DWCD&SS, underscored the need to move beyond awareness towards sustained, result-oriented action to ensure that children with special needs receive equal opportunities for family life, care and belonging. He stated, “Through sustained collaboration among child protection authorities, healthcare professionals and adoption agencies, we must translate our commitment into meaningful outcomes for children.”
The workshop witnessed the participation of officials and representatives from State Adoption Resource Agencies (SARAs), Specialised Adoption Agencies (SAAs), Child Care Institutions (CCIs), District Child Protection Units (DCPUs), Chief Medical Officers (CMOs), Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), healthcare institutions and child protection organisations. The diverse participation enabled a comprehensive examination of the medical, legal, procedural and administrative dimensions of adoption.
Deliberations focused on key challenges relating to medical assessments, legal and procedural requirements, financial considerations, grievance redressal and inter-departmental coordination. Particular emphasis was placed on strengthening linkages between healthcare institutions and child protection systems to facilitate timely medical evaluations, appropriate care planning and smoother adoption processes.
Group discussions provided stakeholders with an opportunity to examine region-specific challenges and formulate practical, actionable and time-bound recommendations. The discussions explored measures to expand outreach, strengthen institutional capacities, address procedural bottlenecks and improve support for children with special needs at every stage of the adoption process.
A short documentary film portraying a successful adoption story involving children with special needs was unveiled during the workshop. Through a compelling real-life narrative, the film highlighted the transformative impact of family-based care, demonstrating how a nurturing family can provide children with security, emotional support, dignity and a lasting sense of belonging.
With the Ranchi workshop, CARA has completed the fifth in its series of Regional Consultative Workshops, following earlier consultations in Rajasthan for the Northern Zone, Assam for the North-Eastern Zone, Madhya Pradesh for the Central Zone and Maharashtra for the Western Zone. Together, these consultations have provided a structured platform to identify region-specific challenges, share effective practices and strengthen collaboration among stakeholders engaged in adoption and child protection.
The recommendations emerging from the Eastern Zone consultation are expected to inform future interventions aimed at improving adoption facilitation, strengthening convergence between healthcare and child protection systems, and expanding family-based rehabilitation opportunities for children with special needs across the country.
Through these consultative initiatives, CARA continues to advance a child-centric and inclusive approach to adoption, reinforcing the principle that every child deserves not just care, but the opportunity to grow up in a family where they are loved, valued and supported.

title: Union MoS Raksha Khadse Highlights Role of India-New Zealand Rugby Series in Advancing Sports Diplomacy and Youth Development
subtitle: Rajgir, Bihar hosts historic U20 series marking 100 years of sporting ties, bringing young athletes together through international competition and cultural exchange
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

content:
Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse addressed the significance of the India–New Zealand U20 Rugby Series in strengthening sports diplomacy, expanding international exposure for young athletes and advancing cooperation in sports development. Held at the Rajgir Sports Complex in Bihar under the 100 Years of Unity through Sport initiative, the series marks a century of sporting ties between India and New Zealand.
The historic India-New Zealand U20 Rugby Series concluded at the Rajgir Sports Complex in Bihar on Tuesday, marking an important milestone in the sporting relationship between the two countries as part of the 100 Years of Unity through Sport initiative.
The event was graced by Shri Samrat Chaudhary, Chief Minister of Bihar, Smt Raksha Khadse, Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India; Ms Shreyasi Singh, Minister of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Bihar; Shri Matt Ayers, Acting High Commissioner of New Zealand in India; Shri Sanjay Mayukh, President, Rugby Football Association of Bihar and Member of Legislative Council - Bihar; and Mr Rahul Bose, President, Rugby India.
100 years of India–New Zealand sporting ties
The series formed part of the 100 Years of Unity through Sport initiative, reflecting the role of sport in strengthening India’s international relationships and cultural connections. Bringing together young athletes from India and New Zealand, the exchange highlighted how sport can serve as a powerful instrument of soft power, fostering mutual understanding, friendship and long-term collaboration between nations.
India–New Zealand U20 Rugby Series Brings Young Athletes Together
Bringing together the U20 men’s and women’s teams from India and New Zealand, the series provided a platform for young athletes to connect through rugby, shared learning and cultural exchange. The programme featured joint training sessions, cultural interactions and four highly-competitive Rugby Sevens matches, including for the first time in history, two mixed-team matches in which national players from two nations played alongside each other, resulting in free-flowing exciting rugby. There can be no better example of sport dissolving boundaries.
Smt Raksha Khadse, Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, said, “Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India continues to strengthen its global engagement through sport, recognising its potential as a powerful instrument of soft power. The India–New Zealand U20 Rugby Series exemplifies how sport can transcend borders, foster mutual understanding and bring nations together through a shared spirit of unity and friendship. As India and New Zealand celebrate 100 years of sporting ties, exchanges such as this demonstrate how sporting partnerships can strengthen bilateral relations, encourage cultural dialogue and create lasting connections between young people across nations.”
Ms Shreyasi Singh, Minister of Sports and Industries, Government of Bihar, said, “Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of Hon’ble Chief Minister of Bihar Shri Samrat Chaudhary, Bihar is committed to strengthening its sporting ecosystem and creating greater opportunities for young athletes. It is a matter of pride for Bihar to host this special India–New Zealand rugby exchange in Rajgir, celebrating 100 years of sporting ties between the two countries. Sport brings people and cultures together, and this series provides young athletes from both nations an opportunity to share experiences, learn from one another and build lasting connections, further strengthening international sporting collaboration and cultural understanding.”
Mr Rahul Bose, President, Rugby India, said, “The India-New Zealand U20 Rugby Series is about much more than the game itself. As we mark 100 years of sporting ties between our countries, bringing these young players together reflects the values that make rugby special: respect, teamwork and friendship. The mixed-team matches were a particularly meaningful part of this exchange, with Indian and New Zealand players standing alongside one another as teammates. We hope the relationships built here in Rajgir will endure and create a foundation for continued collaboration between Rugby India and New Zealand Rugby.”
The visiting New Zealand delegation comprised the U20 men’s team, Tama Toa, and the U20 women’s team, Hine Toa, featuring 24 young Māori players. Their visit provided an opportunity for the players to experience Indian culture while sharing their own traditions and perspectives with their Indian counterparts.
Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation in Rugby Development
The series also builds on the growing collaboration between Rugby India and New Zealand Rugby. In May 2026, Rugby India hosted New Zealand Rugby coaching educators at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar for a coaching development programme involving 35 Indian coaches. The programme focused on strengthening coaching capabilities and supporting the continued development of rugby in India.
As India and New Zealand celebrate a century of sporting ties, the series in Rajgir underscores the power of sport to strengthen bilateral relationships, encourage cultural understanding and create lasting connections between young people. It also reflects the growing role of sport in India’s international engagement, demonstrating how shared sporting experiences can build bridges between nations and contribute to a more connected global sporting community.

title: India firmly committed to clean sport: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya at COP10 Bureau meeting under UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport
subtitle:
“India to bring further amendments to the National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions”: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.

“NADA conducted over 7,000 tests, 350+ awareness sessions and 27,000 participants reached in 2025-26; Know Your Medicine app records over half a million searches”: Union Sports Minister Dr. Mandaviya.
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 3:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya chaired the third formal meeting of the COP10 Bureau and the fourth formal meeting of the Fund’s Approval Committee for 2026–27 under the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport in New Delhi.
Dr. Mandaviya assured the Bureau of India’s commitment to clean sport. He said, “India firmly believes that sporting excellence must always be accompanied by integrity. Every athlete deserves a fair opportunity to compete, with success determined by talent, preparation and hard work, and not by prohibited substances or methods. Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji has regularly emphasised clean sport and the need to practice zero tolerance towards the menace of doping.”
The Union Sports Minister highlighted the strengthening of India’s anti-doping framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment. “India has strengthened its legal and institutional framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment, both of which came into force in July 2026,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “We will also bring another amendment in the next session of our parliament, which aims to introduce criminal provisions to deal with violations even more effectively, including those by coaches and supply chain stakeholders.”
The Union Sports Minister further highlighted the steps India has already taken to tackle doping and inform its athletes about banned substances.
“During 2025-26, the National Anti-Doping Agency of India conducted over 7,000 tests and more than 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching 27,000 participants, while focusing on risk-based testing and intelligence-led investigations,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “The Know Your Medicine mobile application has recorded over half a million searches, supporting informed decisions about medicines.”
Dr. Mandaviya highlighted the forthcoming signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Ministry of Education, and UNESCO to introduce the Sport Values in Every Classroom Toolkit in India. The initiative aims to bring sporting values, ethics and integrity to classrooms and reach millions of young minds.
The meeting aimed to advance global collaboration in the fight against doping and strengthen the Convention’s implementation. Discussions focused on a framework document outlining the roles and responsibilities of public authorities in the global anti-doping ecosystem, as well as strengthening anti-doping education capacity and academic research through engagement with States Parties via the National Compliance Platform. The agenda also covered resource mobilisation, the Fund’s Operational Strategy for 2026-2031, compliance and capacity-building to support a sustainable global anti-doping system.
The inaugural session was attended by Mr. Farid Gayibov, Minister of Youth and Sports of the Republic of Azerbaijan and Chairperson of the COP10 Bureau; Mr. Luke McCann, Chairperson of the Approval Committee of the Fund for the Elimination of Doping in Sport; Mr. Hari Ranjan Rao, Secretary (Sports), Government of India and Vice-Chairperson of the COP10 Bureau; Mr. Gustavo Merino, Director for Social Policies and Inclusion, UNESCO; and members of the COP10 Bureau and the Fund Approval Committee from Zambia, the Kingdom of Spain and the Russian Federation.
The joint meeting reflects India’s engagement in global sports governance, with India representing Group IV as a Vice-Chairperson, and its commitment to advancing ethical sporting practices and supporting international frameworks such as the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport.

title: Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage
subtitle: Powering India's Industries Towards a Net Zero Future
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 OCT 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi
content:
CCUS is an important pathway for reducing emissions from hard-to-abate sectors. Carbon dioxide is increasingly being viewed not only as an emission, but also as a potential resource. CCUS can support India’s Net Zero by 2070 vision while strengthening industrial competitiveness and resource efficiency. The Government is fostering an ecosystem that brings together research institutions, public sector enterprises and private industry. This growing ecosystem spans operational projects, projects under execution and proposed initiatives across multiple States. These efforts are laying the foundation for indigenous CCUS capabilities, carbon utilisation and secure carbon storage.
CCUS
Bridging the Gap in India’s Net Zero Journey
India’s journey towards Net Zero by 2070 requires reducing emissions across its energy and industrial sectors. Renewable energy can significantly lower emissions, but some industrial processes cannot be easily electrified. These include processes requiring very high temperatures or carbon-based inputs.
Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS)
offers an additional pathway for addressing such emissions. It involves capturing carbon dioxide from industrial sources before its release into the atmosphere. The captured carbon dioxide can then be utilised in productive applications or stored securely underground. CCUS can therefore complement renewable energy and support India’s transition towards a lower-carbon industrial economy.
NITI Aayog identifies CCUS as critical for decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors
, including steel, cement, oil and gas, petrochemicals, chemicals and fertilisers. These industries contribute significantly to industrial emissions and face technological challenges in achieving deep decarbonisation. CCUS can help reduce emissions from existing facilities while supporting the continued production of essential goods. It can also create opportunities for developing new technologies, infrastructure and industrial capabilities in India. By connecting carbon capture with utilisation and secure storage, the approach can address emissions across multiple stages. CCUS can thus support India’s climate goals while maintaining industrial growth and economic development.
Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies
ESTIC-2026, the second edition of India’s Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave, is being held from 27–29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Organised by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), the conclave follows the theme “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies.” It advances emerging frontiers in science and technology, including
energy technologies such as Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS
). Spanning 12 thematic areas, ESTIC-2026 features plenary sessions, technical discussions and exhibitions. The conclave also promotes strategic collaborations in support of India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Read More on the agenda:
ESTIC 2026
CCUS Process: From Capture to Storage
Step 1: Capturing Carbon Dioxide at the Source
The process begins at an industrial facility where carbon dioxide is generated. Capture systems separate carbon dioxide from gases released during fuel combustion or industrial processes. The captured gas is then purified, dried and compressed into a dense form before being transported or used.
Step 2: From Capture to Transport
Pipelines are commonly used to transport carbon dioxide over suitable distances. Ships and other transport modes can provide flexibility, especially for longer distances. The choice of transport depends on distance, volume, infrastructure and the destination. The carbon dioxide can then be sent to a utilisation facility or geological storage site.
Did You Know?
A geological storage site is a secure, deep underground location used to permanently isolate captured CO₂. CO₂ geological storage (geo-storage) is a promising approach that can help to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Step 3: Carbon Utilisation and Permanent Storage
At the final stage, captured carbon dioxide can either be put to productive use or stored permanently underground. It can be used in applications such as enhanced oil recovery, food and beverages, urea, green methanol and concrete. For permanent storage, carbon dioxide is injected deep underground into suitable geological formations, including depleted oil and gas reservoirs, deep saline aquifers and basaltic rock formations.
CCUS Hubs and Clusters Model
India’s CCUS framework envisages
regional clusters and hubs
connecting multiple carbon dioxide emitters with shared infrastructure. This model can integrate common systems for carbon dioxide transport, utilisation and storage. Captured carbon dioxide can be collected from multiple sources and transported through shared networks. It can then be directed to suitable utilisation facilities or geological storage sites.
NITI Aayog
identifies the
hub and cluster approach
as suitable for India. The model can create economies of scale, reduce infrastructure risks and connect carbon dioxide supply with potential demand.
The
Department of Science and Technology’s CCUS Roadmap 2025
identifies potential industrial and geological regions for such clusters. These include the
Gujarat coast
, with its concentration of refineries and chemical industries. The
Odisha–Jharkhand belt
offers potential for clusters linked to steel and cement industries.
Northeast India
also presents opportunities linked to its oil and gas resources. Such regional clusters can bring together emitters, transport infrastructure, utilisation facilities and storage sites. This approach can help develop a coordinated CCUS ecosystem suited to India’s industrial landscape.
CCUS Advancing the Low Carbon Transition
India’s low-carbon transition requires solutions that combine economic growth with deeper emission reductions. CCUS addresses this gap by managing carbon dioxide at source and creating opportunities for its reuse. It complements renewable energy expansion while opening applications across industry, hydrogen and carbon dioxide removal.
Decarbonising Hard-to-Abate Sectors
Hard-to-Abate Sectors (steel, cement, refineries/chemicals, fertilisers) release carbon dioxide directly from their processes. Their emissions can be difficult to eliminate through electrification (transition to renewables) alone.
Emissions from these sectors and thermal power generation are expected to reach nearly 2,300 million tonnes per annum by 2030
, making their capture and abatement critical. CCUS technology provides a means of addressing these emissions from ongoing industrial activity.
Did you know?
Green Hydrogen
is produced by electrolysis of water using power generated from renewable energy sources.
Blue Hydrogen
is produced using natural gas or coal as the primary feedstock.
Enabling the Low Carbon Hydrogen Economy
CCUS is expected to play an important part in India’s shift towards hydrogen, through blue hydrogen production using coal gasification coupled with carbon capture. This complements India’s efforts to develop a low-carbon hydrogen economy.
Coal Gasification
Coal gasification converts solid coal into a clean, useful gas using controlled heat. This gas is called
synthesis gas, or syngas
. The process of producing it from coal is known as
coal gasification
. There are two established methods of doing this.
Surface coal gasification
processes mined coal in above-ground gasifiers.
Underground coal gasification
converts coal directly within the underground layer. In both cases, coal is not fully burned, unlike conventional combustion. Instead, it reacts with a limited supply of oxygen and steam. This takes place at high temperatures, typically between 800°C and 1,600°C. These conditions break coal's complex structure into simpler gases.
Sustaining Existing Energy Infrastructure
As of August 2026, fossil-fuel-based sources accounted for 45.12% of India’s total installed power capacity. This existing infrastructure will remain part of India’s energy system during the transition to cleaner sources. Managing emissions from these assets will therefore be important for achieving long-term climate goals. CCUS can support this effort by enabling existing thermal power plants and industries to reduce emissions. Steel and cement facilities can also potentially be retrofitted with CCUS systems. This can reduce carbon dioxide emissions while allowing essential energy and industrial infrastructure to continue operating.
Carbon Utilisation
Within the Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage framework, captured carbon dioxide can serve as a feedstock for materials, fuels, chemicals and biological products, creating pathways for both carbon management and industrial value. Applications include
building materials
such as concrete and aggregates,
synthetic fuels and chemicals
,
polymers
,
enhanced oil recovery
with underground carbon storage, and
algae-based products
including biofuels. These applications extend carbon dioxide utilisation across materials, fuels, chemicals and biological products, while improving resource efficiency.
India’s First of Its Kind CCU Test Beds In Coal- Gasification Facilities
Through one of its recent interventions,
DST has supported two Technology Deployment Testbeds to be implemented by Industry-Research Consortia between IIT Delhi – Thermax Ltd and CSIR-IICT Hyderabad – BHEL
for setting up pilot-scale demonstrations in Coal Gasification plants for Methanol and DME production, with Industry partnering as a solution provider along with a Technology designer (knowledge partner) to deploy CCU in hard-to-abate sectors like Thermal power.
India’s First Integrated CCUS Field Laboratory
India’s first integrated CCUS Field Laboratory at IIT Bombay
, inaugurated in May 2026, brings carbon capture, utilisation and permanent geological storage together on a single pilot-scale platform. The indigenous facility can capture up to
3 tonnes of carbon dioxide per day
from industrial emissions and ambient air, using non-potable water, and convert it into advantageous carbonate and bicarbonate products. Scientific drilling in
Deccan Traps basalt formations
will further assess India’s potential for safe and permanent carbon dioxide storage. The facility provides a
national testbed for developing and scaling indigenous carbon management technologies
, supporting Net Zero 2070 and solutions for hard-to-abate industries. Read more:
India’s First Integrated CCUS Field Laboratory Facility
Strengthening India’s CCUS Ecosystem
The Government of India has undertaken initiatives spanning research, policy and industry to advance CCUS development and reduce emissions. These measures strengthen the foundation for India’s Net Zero target by 2070.
Union Budget 2026–27, CCUS Scheme:
Announced in
February 2026
, the
Ministry of Finance
allocated
₹
20,000 crore over five years
to promote
carbon capture, utilisation and storage
in five major industrial sectors:
Power, Steel, Cement, Refineries, and Chemicals
.
Department of Science & Technology- CCUS R&D Roadmap:
Launched in
December 2025
, the roadmap provides strategic direction for
CCUS research, funding, technology development and deployment
, with a focus on commercial readiness, breakthrough technologies and enabling frameworks.
Click to Access the DST Roadmap
NITI Aayog CCUS Policy Framework & Mechanism:
Released in November 2022, the report examines CCUS as an emissions reduction strategy for deep decarbonisation of hard-to-abate sectors and outlines sector-specific policy interventions for its deployment.
Click to Access NITI Aayog Report
National CCUS Centres:
Established in 2022 at
IIT Bombay and JNCASR, Bengaluru
, with backing from the Department of Science and Technology, these centres focus on CCUS research, technology development, pilot-scale demonstration and industry collaboration.
India’s CCUS Initiative
:
Spearheaded jointly by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), India launched a major research drive on CCUS. As part of
Mission Innovation
, a global clean energy platform, India collaborated with 13 partner countries to advance technologies to capture, separate, safely store, and convert CO2 into useful value-added materials.
India Launches First Ever CCU Testbed Cluster for Cement Industry
India launched its
first cluster of five Carbon Capture and Utilisation
testbeds for the
cement industry
on 11th May 2025. Led by the
Department of Science and Technology
(DST), the initiative brings leading cement companies and premier research institutions together under a Public-Private Partnership model to develop and deploy industrial CCU technologies. The testbeds cover applications ranging from carbon dioxide capture and mineralisation to its conversion into concrete products, advancing practical CCU applications for cement sector decarbonisation.
India Accelerates on CCU
India has several CCU projects as of April 2026, spanning operational, under execution and proposed stages. The portfolio includes public sector enterprises, private industry, and academic institutions across multiple States. Projects focus on reducing carbon emissions, productive carbon utilisation and circular economy applications.
Operational:
Three projects are operational, with one each in
Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra
.
Under Construction/Execution:
Six projects are under construction or execution.
Andhra Pradesh leads with three projects
, followed by
Telangana with two
and
Maharashtra with one
.
Proposed:
Sixteen projects are at the proposed stage.
Assam and Odisha lead with four projects each
, followed by
Gujarat and Rajasthan with two each
. Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Tamil Nadu have one project each.
The project pipeline reflects growing momentum towards carbon management solutions across India. It also provides a foundation for scaling indigenous Carbon Capture and Utilisation applications.
Shaping India’s Low Carbon Industrial Future
India’s Panchamrit commitments provide the broader context for advancing low-carbon growth and achieving Net Zero by 2070. CCUS adds an important technology dimension by addressing emissions from sectors where complete elimination remains challenging. Government initiatives spanning research, technology development, financing and demonstration are creating the foundations for wider deployment. As these efforts progress, CCUS could improve resource efficiency, support industrial decarbonisation, and help develop a more circular carbon economy.
